title: Salesforce API review: what API access costs
snippet:
Everyone asks what the Salesforce API costs and gets told it is free, which is true in the sense that there is no charge per call and false in the sense that matters. On Pro Suite, Salesforce prices the Web Services API as an add-on at $25 per user per month on top of a $100 seat. From Core at $195 a seat it is bundled. Starter Suite and Free Suite are not on the rate-limit table at all.

Salesforce API pricing is really edition pricing, and the API is the feature that moves between editions. Salesforce lists six Sales Cloud tiers. The one that matters for an integration is the step from Pro Suite to Core, because that is where the Web Services API stops being an add-on.
### Starter Suite

### Pro Suite

### Core

/user/mo

- Forecasting, opportunity scoring, conversation intelligence

### Advanced
$395
/user/mo

### Max
$550
/user/mo

- The complete suite
Prices are the published US rate per user per month, billed monthly or annually. There is also a Free Suite at $0, which like Starter Suite does not appear on the API allocation table. Add-ons are priced separately on top: Agentforce for Sales from $125 per user per month, Sales Programs from $100, Revenue Intelligence from $220, Revenue Cloud from $200 and Partner Relationship Management from $10 per login per month.

| Edition | Calls per Salesforce license | Daily org total | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise, or Professional with API access enabled | 1,000 | 100,000 + licenses x 1,000 | 15 licenses gives 115,000 a day |
| Unlimited and Performance | 5,000 | 100,000 + licenses x 5,000 | 15 licenses gives 175,000 a day |
| Developer Edition | n/a | 15,000 | Flat, and free to build against |
| Full Sandbox | n/a | 5,000,000 | Unless it was created from a template |
| Salesforce Platform license | 1,000 | Counts the same as a full license | Lightning Platform One App gives 200 |
| Partner or Customer Community | 0 to 200 | Login licenses give 10 | Community seats are not an API budget |

title: Salesforce API: Types, Access and Limits (2026 Guide)
snippet:
> The token's issued, the request's well formed, and the response's a refusal because the edition or the user's permissions don't allow API use. Syntax's rarely the cause.
- Enterprise: API access included
- Unlimited: API access included
- Developer: API access included
- Performance: API access included
- Professional: **API access only as a paid add-on**
- Essentials: no API access

You pay nothing per individual call, because Salesforce meters a rolling 24-hour allocation of requests per org; that allocation's the budget your `Remaining` reading's drawn from.
To see how much headroom your batch has before it competes with everything else in the org, read the base allowance for each org type in the table.
| Org type | Base API requests per 24 hours |
|---|---|
| Developer | 15,000 |
| Enterprise / Professional | 100,000 |
| Unlimited / Performance | 100,000 |
| Full Sandbox | 5,000,000 |

According to [Salescrew / GetOneProfile](https://getoneprofile.ai/tools/salesforce-api-rate-limits), a [Developer](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/resources-composite-sobjects-collections-update.html) org gets 15,000 calls, so a sync that touches 20,000 records one call at a time fails before the day is out.
Enterprise/Pro and Unlimited/Performance both start at 100,000, which means moving up an edition doesn't by itself raise the base figure.
**5,000,000 is what Full Sandbox allows**, so a load test there says nothing about whether the same job fits in production.
Not every tier is in the table; the allowance is shared across every integration in the org, not per app.

### Is the Salesforce API free to use?
There's no separate charge per call, but access comes with the edition you already pay for, and **every call draws on the org's daily allowance**.
A failed call can still spend that allowance, so a looping step costs you capacity even when it returns nothing useful.
If you need more room, the route's a purchase through your Salesforce account team, not a setting you can toggle.
### Does a Salesforce Developer Edition org include API access?
Yes. Developer Edition is a free test org that ships with API access enabled, so you can build and test the whole flow there at no cost.
Because its daily allowance's small, a load test in that org will hit the ceiling long before it tells you anything about production.
Before you plan around a paid edition, confirm API access: Professional, among others, treats it as an add-on.
